subject: chemistry
title: Condensation polymerisation
key_idea: (AQA: Higher tier) (Separate science) Condensation polymerisation uses monomers with two functional groups each. They join in a chain and usually lose a small molecule such as water each time a link forms. A diol and a dicarboxylic acid make a polyester.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) (Separate science) Condensation polymerisation involves monomers with two functional groups. When they react they join together and usually lose a small molecule such as water.

items.meaning: Monomers with two functional groups join in a chain, losing a small molecule each time.
A condensation polymer made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid.
The link –COO– formed when a –COOH group reacts with an –OH group.

items: A diol has an –OH group at each end of the molecule.
A dicarboxylic acid has a –COOH group at each end.
The simplest polymers use two different monomers, each with two of the same functional group. Each monomer needs at least two, so the chain can grow at both ends.
Ethanediol and hexanedioic acid make a polyester.

blocks.text: Each time an ester link forms, one molecule of water is made. The –OH of the acid group and an H from the alcohol group make the water.
Because each monomer has a functional group at both ends, the chain can keep growing. Block diagrams show the pattern.

diagram.alt: Steps in forming an ester link and growing a polyester chain.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of forming a polyester in order.
steps: A –COOH group on one monomer meets an –OH group on the other monomer.
A molecule of water is formed and lost.
An ester link joins the two monomers.
Each end of the new molecule still has a functional group.
More monomers join at both ends.
A long polyester chain is formed.

items: The repeating unit contains one diol and one dicarboxylic acid.
Water is lost at every ester link, so the repeating unit does not have the same atoms as the two monomers.

Two different monomers, each with two functional groups
None. The polymer is the only product
Yes, a small molecule such as water (or HCl)

items: (AQA: Higher tier) Condensation monomers have two functional groups each.
A diol and a dicarboxylic acid make a polyester and water.
One water molecule forms for every ester link.

checks.q: (AQA: Higher tier) What is made, apart from a polyester, when a diol reacts with a dicarboxylic acid?
checks.a: Water, one molecule for each ester link formed.

checks.q: (AQA: Higher tier) Why is the formation of a polyester called condensation polymerisation?
checks.a: The monomers join together and lose a small molecule (water) each time a link forms.

checks.q: (AQA: Higher tier) Give two differences between the monomers of addition polymers and condensation polymers.
checks.a: Addition monomers are all the same and have a C=C. Condensation monomers are two different molecules, each with two functional groups.

worked_example.question:
The outer skin of surfboards contains a type of polyester.

Why does this type of polyester melt when it is heated?
answer_points: It has no cross-links (the intermolecular forces are weak).
worked_example.tip: One mark for the type of polymer and one mark for no cross-links.

blocks.text: Some polyesters soften and melt when heated. They are called thermosoftening polymers.

items: They have no cross-links between the chains.
The forces between the chains are weak, so the chains can move past each other.

worked_example.question:
Poly(phenylethene) is an addition polymer.
Polyesters are condensation polymers.
Describe the differences between the type of monomer molecules used to form addition polymers and the type of monomer molecules used to form condensation polymers.
answer_points: Addition: only one monomer, and the monomer is an alkene (unsaturated, has C=C).
One monomer is a (di)alcohol and one is a (di)carboxylic acid, and each monomer molecule has two functional groups, one at each end.
worked_example.tip: Addition monomers can score up to 2 marks and condensation monomers up to 2 marks, to a maximum of 3.

worked_example.question:
Nylon is another polymer formed in a condensation polymerisation reaction.
Nylon can be made from hexanedioyl dichloride and hexane-1,6-diamine.
Both chemicals are highly corrosive.
A solvent is needed which is highly flammable.

Describe how to make nylon in a laboratory.
answer_points: Pour the hexanedioyl dichloride on top of the diamine solution, so that mixing is minimised (using a glass rod, or pouring down the side of the beaker).
Pick up the film of nylon at the interface of the layers with tweezers.
Lift and draw out a thread of nylon slowly, then wash it to remove the corrosive chemicals.
worked_example.tip: Any three of the five points score one mark each.

extra.heading: OCR only: making nylon in the laboratory

blocks.text: Nylon is a polyamide made by condensation polymerisation. It forms where two solutions meet.

items.text: Pour the hexanedioyl dichloride solution carefully on top of the diamine solution to minimise mixing.
A film of nylon forms where the two solutions meet.
Pick it up with tweezers and draw out a thread of nylon slowly.
Wash the thread to remove corrosive chemicals.

items: Wear gloves and eye protection, because the reagents are corrosive.
Avoid naked flames, because the solvent is highly flammable.
Work in a well ventilated lab or fume cupboard, because of fumes.
Hexanedioyl dichloride and hexane-1,6-diamine lose hydrogen chloride, HCl, at each link, not water.
